combats.encounter: Two living statues in the university entrance garden

entries.summary: Soul-sights the two CR 15 statues: Charisma is strongest, Strength weakest; blindness and incapacitation remain possible. Their stated immunities cover charm, exhaustion, fear, grapple, paralysis, petrification, poison, prone, restraint and stun. Runs at a statue, bonus-action dashes after its teleport, then redirects after the other teleports. Finally makes two staff attacks: a natural 1 misses; 16 hits for 14 damage. Cannot apply his usual aura strikes.
Teleports away as Kenzo raises his arm to attack; Kenzo uses his bonus-action dash to pursue the other statue.
Also teleports when pursued. Both reactions are now spent; Kenzo uses his remaining movement to return and make his attacks.

Teleports away from Kenzo without provoking an opportunity attack. Its sorrow forces Wisdom saves: Kenzo succeeds with 24; Delwath succeeds using Favored by the Gods. Wellby, Riswynn and Seeker fail; attacks against them gain advantage. Inspiration does not rescue Wellby or Riswynn. Attacks Wellby: a 17 misses, while 22 and 21 hit; first psychic damage is stated as 29 then followed by an isolated “49,” and the second hit deals 25 psychic.
entries.note: The source does not explicitly resolve whether “49” corrects the first 29-damage statement. No definite first-hit total is chosen.

entries.summary: Attacks Riswynn with the sorrow advantage: a natural 20 critical and a second hit (30 to hit), dealing 49 psychic on the first and 22 on the second. The 30 is corrected from damage to the attack total.
Casts 5th-level Summon Construct, choosing a medium stone construct near the closer/left statue with stony lethargy. Abandons the proposed psychic spell.
Attempts its first attack; the target teleports. Moves 30 feet to close again; no hit or damage is resolved.

entries.actor: Living statue targeted by the construct
entries.summary: Teleports at the construct’s attack, choosing a position within 30 feet; the construct then follows.

Uses Steady Aim and shoots the wounded upper statue with advantage for 23 damage after sacrificing 3d6 sneak damage. It fails DC 18 Dexterity and is blinded. Boots of Speed activation is withdrawn because Steady Aim already used the bonus action; he stays put.

Moves without entering Riswynn’s planned blast, bonus-action Hunter’s Marks one statue, and casts Synaptic Static on both. Both fail DC 19 Intelligence, take 20 damage, and subtract 1d6 from attacks; later clarification also includes ability checks and concentration saves, not other saving throws.

Casts 8th-level Sunburst positioned to catch both statues without the party. Both fail Constitution saves, take 53 radiant damage each and are blinded, with end-of-turn Constitution saves to end blindness. Blindness gives attacks against them advantage.
Repeat Wisdom saves against sorrow. Riswynn succeeds and ends her sorrow vulnerability; Seeker and Wellby remain affected.

Attacks the upper blinded statue with advantage, whose reaction is unavailable. Two staff hits deal 14 and 13 damage; three unarmed hits deal 15, 8 and 11. It becomes bloodied and cracks under the attacks.

Attacks Wellby twice for 29 and 19 psychic. Sorrow advantage and blindness disadvantage cancel. Its blindness prevents the sight-dependent bonus action, and it fails the Constitution save to end blindness.

Attacks Seeker twice with straight rolls as sorrow and blindness cancel; Synaptic Static subtraction is checked and still leaves both hits. Deals 39 and 37 psychic. Both statues fail their repeat effect saves and remain blinded.
Attempts Polymorph into a lizard; the statue succeeds on Wisdom with 26, so no transformation occurs. Synaptic Static does not lower this save.
Moves to the bloodied statue and makes two force slams, both hitting at 23, for 28 total damage. The statue is badly cracked with an arm hanging loose.
Attempts to teleport from the construct’s attack, but blindness leaves no visible destination, so it cannot teleport.
Activates Boots of Speed and moves 90 feet out of the cover created by Kenzo and the construct. Shoots the blinded bloodied statue with advantage; 31 hits for 35 damage, destroying it.
Spends two sorcery points to cast Fount of Moonlight as a bonus action, then hits the remaining blinded statue three times with advantage for 86 total damage, bloodying it.
entries.note: The DM says “Wellby’s sword” at u1035, but the surrounding turn ownership and Delwath’s damage declaration identify Delwath’s attacks.

entries.summary: Casts Guiding Bolt with advantage for 28 damage; the remaining statue survives and stays blind.

Attacks the remaining blinded statue with advantage: first staff attack is a natural 20 for 18 damage, second hits for 9, then unarmed hits deal 7 and 15. The torso collapses and it falls in half. A further natural-20 roll is mentioned after the collapse; no additional resolved hit is counted.

ending.summary: Both living statues collapse; the party can proceed into the Faculty of Natural History ruins. Riswynn’s Sunburst is credited with shutting down their sight-dependent powers. Subsequent healing and exploration are outside the combat segment.
